months.note: 국내에서 기록된 달이며, 주로 서해안의 하구·간척지와 섬에서 관찰되었다.

summary: 적은 수가 우리나라에서 겨울을 나며, 평야의 트인 땅이나 습지에 산다. 알타이, 파미르, 티베트, 히말라야 등지에서 번식한다. 번식지에서는 4월 무렵 한배에 보통 알 3개를 낳는다.

points.en: dark brown tail with pale bands

sexes.text: 암수 생김새가 같고 암컷이 훨씬 크다.

young: 어린새는 어른새보다 아랫면의 갈색 세로무늬가 훨씬 굵고 빽빽해 더 어둡게 보이고, 납막과 다리가 노란색이 아니라 푸른빛이 도는 회색이다.

art.subject: Saker Falcon (Falco cherrug), adult in winter: crown and nape whitish-buff with fine brown streaks, a pale supercilium, a thin dark line behind the eye and a narrow, often faint dark moustache on a whitish cheek; mantle, scapulars and wing coverts dark earth-brown with rufous-buff fringes; flight feathers darker brown; underparts white to creamy with dark brown teardrop streaks and spots, heaviest on the flanks and thighs; tail brown with pale buff oval spots forming bars; bill bluish-grey with a dark tip; bare yellow cere and eye-ring; dark brown eye; legs yellow.
art.pose: perched on a low mound in open country, side view
art.scene: Korean winter plain: open flat farmland beside a wetland; no people, buildings or text
views: adult, side view perched upright on a low mound: whitish-buff crown with fine brown streaks, faint thin moustache, dark brown back and wings with rufous-buff fringes, white underparts with dark brown teardrop streaks, long tail beyond the wingtips, yellow legs
adult, in flight seen from below: whitish body with dark brown streaks, dark underwing coverts and armpits contrasting with paler barred flight feathers, long brown tail with pale bands
art.build: Large, powerful falcon, 46cm, much larger than a Common Kestrel and larger than a Peregrine Falcon. Head fairly large and flat-crowned; bill short, strongly hooked, much shorter than the head. Legs yellow, fairly short, with strong toes. At rest the wingtips fall clearly short of the tail tip, reaching about three-quarters of the way down it. Tail rather long. In flight broad-based pointed wings, the dark underwing coverts contrasting with paler flight feathers.
avoid: Do not paint a black hood, a broad black moustache or a blue-grey back; those are Peregrine Falcon (Falco peregrinus).
Do not paint barred underparts; the Saker's underparts are streaked and spotted.
Do not make the wingtips reach the tail tip at rest; the tail clearly projects beyond them.
Do not paint a dark crown; the crown is pale.
